subject: Observability telemetry throttling & SLAs for ACME VPC deploy
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Observability telemetry throttling & SLAs for ACME VPC deploy

Hi Liam / Avery,

Thanks for taking this on. As we approach the VPC handoff for the ACME private deployment, we want to align on telemetry throughput, transient buffering behavior, and minimum SLA windows for logs/metrics/traces into your SIEM. Key asks from our side: 

- Confirm max sustained ingest (events/sec) your SIEM cluster can accept from a single forwarder IP.
- Any egress/throttling rules on your firewall that would close idle TCP connections after N seconds (this affects persistent collectors).
- Required retention/immutability windows for audit logs (we typically ship short-lived debug logs plus compacted audit records).

Attached: redwood-telemetry-sample-payloads.json (example compacted events), and a proposed handshake-telemetry-config.yaml with suggested buffer sizes and backpressure behavior.

Proposal (high level):
- Persistent TLS connection from our forwarder to your HEC endpoint, keepalive every 30s.
- Local buffer with capped disk spool up to 4GB per forwarder; backpressure to reduce sampling to 1% when spool > 3GB.
- Trace spans: stream at low-priority channel with 10s flush interval; critical audit events stream immediately.

Can you confirm if the above fits ACME constraints? If not, list the hard limits and we’ll adapt.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if useful.

— Rishi

Subject: Re: Observability telemetry throttling & SLAs for ACME VPC deploy

Rishi,

Appreciate the detailed starter. A few constraints on our side:

- Our Splunk HEC frontends accept ~18k events/sec per ingest node; production frontends are behind a load balancer. We’d prefer clients keep sustained open connections and do not open a new TCP per request.
- Firewall: idle TCP sessions are closed after 120s of inactivity. Keepalives at 30s are fine.
- Disk policy: we cannot accept more than 2GB per single forwarder spool on the appliance; larger buffers must be split across multiple forwarders (we can provision additional forwarders if needed).
- Retention: audit logs need 365d retention with immutability flag; debug/traces can be sampled down to 5% and retained 90d.

I’ve attached our SIEM capacity worksheet for reference (acme-siem-capacity-v1.xlsx).

Question: how does Redwood handle burst spikes from model debug logs (e.g., a 10x increase for a short window)? Can your forwarder rate-limit and drop non-critical traces based on dynamic policy?

— Liam
Liam O'Connor
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, AcmeHealth
infra-team@acmehealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <infra-team@acmehealth.com>, Avery Singh <ops+audit@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Apr 2029 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability telemetry throttling & SLAs for ACME VPC deploy

Liam / Avery — thanks for the quick note and the capacity sheet. We discussed internally and here’s a concrete handshake we can put in the runbook: 

1) Connection model
- Single persistent TLS connection per forwarder, with TLS renegotiation disabled. Keepalive ping every 30s.

2) Buffering and burst handling
- Local spool: 2GB per forwarder by default (matches ACME max). If customer wants >2GB, request additional forwarder allocation.
- Burst behavior: if incoming rate > 10x baseline, the forwarder will:
  - Step 1: enable aggressive sampling on non-audit traces (reduce to 5% immediately).
  - Step 2: if spool > 75%, start dropping debug-level logs older than 60s (non-audit).
  - Step 3: if spool hits 100%, circuit-breaker opens and system will emit an immediate critical audit event to the "audit" channel and pause non-critical telemetry until spool falls below 50%.

3) SLA windows and retention flags
- Audit events: delivered with at-least-once guarantee; marked immutable on ingest; retained 365d.
- Traces: best-effort streaming; default retention 90d; sampling policy is adjustable per deployment.

4) Payloads and sample rate
- See attached redwood-telemetry-sample-payloads.json for compact event layout. We will provide a small schema diff for the audit channel to match your SIEM mapping.

5) Operational hooks
- Health endpoint: forwarder exposes /health and /metrics on localhost; Redwood will ship a startup manifest for customer sidecar monitoring.
- Debug mode: 10m debug window controlled via signed URL (requires ACME ops approval).

Action items:
- Liam: confirm you can provision one additional forwarder for peak testing (we’ll simulate 25k eps bursts).
- Avery: confirm the required immutability flag name and any required headers your SIEM expects on ingest.

If that all sounds ok we’ll fold this into the VPC runbook and provide a small test harness (curl + sample payloads) that you can run in staging.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
